Subject: Acme - pricing & context-length profiling follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap + actions from my side so we can put together an accurate pricing estimate: 

Recap:
- Primary use cases you mentioned: customer support chat (real-time, multi-turn), long-form document summarization, and document QA/search over legal/finance docs.
- Peak concurrency: ~40 simultaneous sessions during morning hours.
- Monthly active users: roughly 12k.

Open items I need to confirm to model pricing:
1) Average "prompt" tokens and average "completion" tokens per request (you were estimating ranges but if you can confirm averages that helps): e.g., support chat avg prompt ~200 / completion ~300.
2) Token distribution by context-length requirement: percent of requests that require default (<=8k), extended (32k), and very long (128k).
3) Estimated monthly token volume (or range) and an internal target for $/1M tokens to guide tradeoffs (we commonly model $/1M for committed vs on-demand pricing).

I've attached a short survey (acme_context_length_survey.csv) with the fields above if you want to fill it out — it takes 5 minutes. Once I have the numbers I'll run a short model to show: expected monthly token counts, projected unit cost across 8k/32k/128k profiles, and a suggested pricing tier that meets your target economics.

Suggested next steps:
- You fill the survey or reply with the three items above (avg prompt/completion, % by context size, monthly token estimate).
- I’ll produce a 1-page cost estimate and a glidepath recommendation (e.g., mostly 8k + burst to 32k for 10% of requests) and share a draft pricing worksheet.

Attachments: acme_context_length_survey.csv (text/csv)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the survey. I filled in the high-level estimates below so you can get started: 

Quick answers (high confidence):
- Average prompt tokens (all use cases, weighted avg): ~320 tokens
- Average completion tokens: ~480 tokens
- Estimated monthly token volume (mid): ~120,000,000 tokens/month (range 80M - 180M)

Context-length distribution (approx):
- <=8k: 88% (mostly short chat and typical summarization)
- 32k: 10% (multi-doc summarization / long legal Q&A)
- 128k: 2% (quarterly compliance report ingestion + very long legal records)

Budget & unit economics:
- Current internal budget for LLM infra: ~$2,500 - $7,000/month (we know this is low today; we're trying to scale predictability).
- Target $/1M tokens for procurement discussions: ~$25-$30 per 1M tokens (target to keep costs predictable while we scale).

We can share a couple sample transcripts if helpful (redact PII). Priya and I are both copied. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow if you want to walk through assumptions.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Analytics
alex.j@acmeanalytics.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme - pricing & context-length profiling follow-up

Alex / Priya — great, thanks for the numbers. I've put together an initial profiling summary below and attached a pricing worksheet (redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx) with line items for 8k/32k/128k split and committed vs on-demand unit costs. Highlights and assumptions so we're aligned: 

Assumptions (from your inputs):
- Weighted avg prompt tokens: 320
- Weighted avg completion tokens: 480
- Monthly tokens (mid): 120M
- Context split: 88% 8k, 10% 32k, 2% 128k

Use-case breakouts (examples & token profiles):
- Support chat (multi-turn): ~180 prompt / ~350 completion (avg conversation length 6 turns per session). Represents ~60% of requests.
- Document summarization (single-doc): ~1,200 prompt / ~600 completion. Represents ~25% of requests.
- Long-form legal ingest & QA: variable; when 32k/128k used, prompt can be 8k-40k depending on chunking; completion 300-1,500 tokens. ~15% of token volume due to long context (but smaller percent of requests).

Projected monthly token breakdown (approx):
- 8k path (88% of requests): ~105.6M tokens/month
- 32k path (10%): ~12M tokens/month
- 128k path (2%): ~2.4M tokens/month

Pricing sensitivity (illustrative):
- If target is $25 / 1M tokens and we model on-demand-like unit economics, monthly cost ~= $3,000 (120M / 1M * $25 = $3,000). 
- Long-context (32k/128k) typically has a 1.5x-3x execution premium due to memory & batching inefficiencies; that will push effective blended $/1M up if significant volume moves to 32k/128k.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) I’ll produce two formal pricing scenarios in the attached worksheet: (A) on-demand blended at your target $25/1M (note: likely needs committed volume to achieve), and (B) committed tier with a pilot discount for months 1–3 and explicit long-context add-on pricing.
2) Confirm whether you want Redwood to propose a Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity) vs hosted committed pricing — Dedicated gives predictable latency and usually better $/1M for sustained heavy usage.
3) If you can share 2–3 redacted transcripts (support & summarization), I can fine-tune the avg token numbers and update the worksheet.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Let me know which option you'd like us to model first and I’ll loop in our pricing lead. If helpful, I can share a one-page summary for your procurement team.

Best,
Marissa
